items.title: Hillcrest mixed-use project, development permit review
items.summary: Reviews building height, parking, and street-level design for a six-story mixed-use proposal.
items.stakes: Neighbors of the Hillcrest site: building height and parking decisions affect shade, traffic, and street parking.

items.title: Bylaws update
items.summary: Updates meeting notice rules and officer terms.
items.stakes: Planning group members: the bylaws set meeting notice rules and officer terms.

meetings.title: Economic Development and Intergovernmental Relations Committee

items.title: Street repaving contract amendment, Districts 3 and 6
items.summary: Adds $4.2 million to the existing arterial paving contract for Districts 3 and 6.
items.stakes: Drivers and bus riders on the listed arterials: the $4.2 million pays for repaving, which likely means lane closures on those streets.

items.title: Weekend construction hours, noise ordinance update
items.summary: Sets a Saturday construction window that starts at 8 a.m. and adds a 48-hour permit notice.
items.stakes: Neighbors of construction sites: Saturday work could start at 8 a.m. and requires 48 hours' notice to nearby residents.

items.title: Balboa Park north entrance: trail and lighting funding
items.summary: Allocates $650,000 for trail repairs and lighting at the north entrance.
items.stakes: People who use the north entrance of Balboa Park: the $650,000 pays for trail repairs and lighting there.

items.title: Budget amendment: move reserves to road and sidewalk repair
items.summary: Moves $18 million from reserves to road and sidewalk repair. The staff summary is linked from the item page.
items.stakes: Anyone who depends on road and sidewalk repair: $18 million moves out of reserves for those repairs, so reserves shrink by that amount.

items.title: Short-term rental permit enforcement update
items.summary: Informational report on complaints, inspections, and permit revocations citywide.
items.stakes: Neighbors of short-term rentals: the report summarizes complaints and permit actions and does not change any rule.

items.title: Behavioral health beds, North County campus
items.summary: Approves operating funds for 40 short-term behavioral health beds.
items.stakes: People in North County who need short-term behavioral health care: the 40 beds would be funded to open.

items.title: Library hours restored at rural branches
items.summary: Restores weekend hours at six rural branch libraries.
items.stakes: Rural library users: weekend hours return at six branches.

items.title: Council public comment rules
items.summary: Proposes changing general public comment from three minutes to two, and scheduled items from two minutes to three.
items.stakes: Anyone who speaks at council: general public comment would drop from three minutes to two if the rule is adopted.

items.title: Affordable housing fee waiver, 5th Avenue project
items.summary: Waives certain impact fees for 84 affordable units.
items.stakes: Developers and future tenants of 84 affordable units: the waived fees lower the cost of building them.

items.title: Annual stormwater permit report
items.summary: Staff reports on runoff inspections and on sites with repeated violations, with a map by council district.
items.stakes: Businesses and homes near sites with repeat runoff violations: the report can lead to inspections and enforcement.

items.title: Park cleanup volunteer program
items.summary: Summarizes volunteer hours and proposes a neighborhood cleanup grant.
items.stakes: Volunteers and neighborhood groups: the program funds cleanup grants that groups can apply for.

items.title: Winter shelter capacity contract, 2026-27 season
items.summary: Adds 600 winter shelter beds across county-contracted sites.
items.stakes: People without shelter this winter: 600 winter beds would be added at county-contracted sites.

items.title: Regional parks and trails maintenance report
items.summary: Annual maintenance backlog report with a list of trails scheduled for repair.
items.stakes: People who use county trails: the report lists which trails are scheduled for repair.

items.title: Park Boulevard corridor plan: presentation
items.summary: City staff presents the corridor plan for bike lanes, crossings, and parking changes, and asks for comments.
items.stakes: Cyclists, drivers, and businesses on Park Boulevard: the plan would change bike lanes, crossings, and parking.

items.title: Short-term rental complaints report
items.summary: Code enforcement report on complaints in the planning area over the last quarter.
items.stakes: Neighbors of short-term rentals: the report shows complaint volume in the planning area.

items.title: Officer elections
items.summary: Election of chair and vice chair for the coming year.
items.stakes: Planning group members: the election picks who leads and speaks for the group next year.

items.title: Council public comment rules (continued from Nov 16)
items.summary: Second reading of the speaking time rules. Staff proposes two minutes for general comment and three minutes for scheduled items.
items.stakes: Everyone who wants to speak at council meetings: if the rule passes, the new time limits apply at future meetings.

items.title: Traffic calming, 30th Street between Upas and University
items.summary: Approves the design and $1.1 million for speed humps, a crossing signal, and a pilot bike lane.
items.stakes: Drivers, people walking, and bike riders on 30th Street: humps, a crossing signal, and a pilot bike lane would be built.

items.title: Outreach funding for recognized community planning groups
items.summary: Proposes annual outreach funding for recognized planning groups, including translation support.
items.stakes: Community planning groups and their neighbors: the funding would pay for notices and translation for outreach.

items.title: Recommendation on the Park Boulevard corridor plan
items.summary: Vote on a recommendation to the City on the corridor plan.
items.stakes: Residents along Park Boulevard: the group's recommendation goes to the City with its vote count.

items.title: Holiday open house and outreach plan
items.summary: Plans a December open house and a schedule for flyers and online notices.
items.stakes: Neighbors who want to hear about group decisions: the plan sets how notices reach them.

items.title: Police response times by council district
items.summary: Staff proposes a monthly response-time report by council district, starting in January.
items.stakes: Residents who call for police help: a monthly report would show response times by council district.

items.title: Accessory dwelling unit impact fee study
items.summary: Directs staff to return with fee options that treat units under 800 square feet differently.
items.stakes: People planning to build small homes: the study could change the fees for units under 800 square feet.

items.title: Six-month transit fare pilot on County routes
items.summary: Proposes reduced fares for youth and seniors on county-operated routes for six months.
items.stakes: Youth and seniors who ride county routes: fares would drop for six months if the pilot passes.

items.title: Emergency medical services contract renewal
items.summary: Renews the ambulance services contract for three years with a new response-time standard.
items.stakes: Anyone who calls for an ambulance: the contract sets a new response-time standard for three years.

meeting_source_note: City Clerk calendar, as listed on the page checked 2026-11-18. The page is undated. Two-week recesses (Nov 2-4, Nov 23-27, Nov 30) have no meetings. Agenda items are not in this data set: the agenda portal lists meeting names and dates only.
